security_audit.summary: Static findings are false positives caused by Markdown Bash examples and inline shell guidance. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent was found; the only remaining risk is the broad Bash tool permission declared by the skill.

remediation.suggestion: Document when Bash commands may run, and require user confirmation for mutating or environment-inspecting commands.
Keep examples clearly labeled as templates and warn users to review commands before running them in a project.

content.user_title: Improve Bash Scripts With Safer Patterns
content.value_statement: Bash scripts often fail silently or break on edge cases. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward safer templates, validation, and testing habits.
actual_capabilities: Provides a standard Bash script template with strict mode, usage text, and trap handling.
Recommends quoting, readonly constants, local variables, and meaningful exit codes.
Shows reusable helpers for error, info, and warning messages.
Describes input validation for required values and numeric arguments.
Covers file checks, array handling, ShellCheck review, and simple function tests.
Highlights common Bash anti-patterns with safer alternatives.
limitations: Does not run ShellCheck by itself; the agent must use available tools.
Targets Bash scripts and does not guarantee compatibility with other shells.
Examples are templates and require project-specific review before use.
Cannot verify runtime behavior without running tests in the target environment.

use_cases.title: Create Reliable Automation Scripts
use_cases.description: Generate Bash script structure with strict mode, parameter handling, and clear usage output.

use_cases.title: Review Existing Shell Scripts
use_cases.description: Check quoting, error handling, file operations, and validation before scripts enter shared repositories.

use_cases.title: Teach Bash Safety Standards
use_cases.description: Use concise examples to explain safer Bash patterns during code review or onboarding.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Bash script for this task. Include strict mode, usage text, required argument validation, and clear success or error messages.

prompt_templates.title: Review Script Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Bash script for quoting, undefined variables, error handling, file checks, and ShellCheck concerns. Prioritize the highest-risk issues.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Automation Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this automation script for safer defaults, idempotent file operations, clearer exit codes, and maintainable helper functions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Tested Release Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Bash release script plan with validation steps, rollback considerations, logging, test strategy, and commands that require confirmation.

output_examples.input: User asks for a new Bash backup script with one required directory argument.
output_examples.output: The assistant returns a structured script outline with strict mode, usage text, input validation, file checks, and clear status messages.

output_examples.input: User asks for a review of a deployment script before sharing it with a team.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists risks by priority, including missing quotes, weak error handling, unsafe file writes, and ShellCheck follow-up tasks.

output_examples.input: User asks how to test a Bash helper function.
output_examples.output: The assistant suggests focused test cases, expected results, failure cases, and how to report readable test failures.

best_practices: Use strict mode, quote variables, and validate required arguments before running main logic.
Keep file operations explicit, checked, and reversible where possible.
Run ShellCheck and project-specific tests before using generated scripts in automation.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated shell commands without reviewing paths, inputs, and side effects.
Do not mix Bash guidance into scripts that must run under plain POSIX sh.
Do not silence errors or ignore failing commands in deployment or cleanup scripts.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI assistants create and review Bash scripts using safer structure, validation, and error handling patterns.

faq.question: Does it execute scripts automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples, but the agent may have Bash tool access depending on the host configuration.

faq.question: Is ShellCheck required?
faq.answer: ShellCheck is not required, but the skill recommends it because it catches many common Bash mistakes.

faq.question: Can it support POSIX sh scripts?
faq.answer: It focuses on Bash. Ask for POSIX compatibility explicitly if your script must avoid Bash-only features.

faq.question: What should I review before running generated scripts?
faq.answer: Review paths, variables, file writes, command substitutions, network calls, and any commands that change system state.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Developers, DevOps engineers, and technical leads who want consistent Bash script structure and safer review habits.
